_comment: Hand-written: iconic item per first-level area, keyed by the geoBoundaries ADM1 shapeName, and optional hand-picked district items keyed by the ADM2 shapeName. tools/build_countries.py merges this into data/countries/MYS.json.

Johor.lore: Malaysia's pineapple heartland around Pontian, at the southern tip of the peninsula; the causeway crosses to Singapore.

Kedah.lore: The 'Rice Bowl of Malaysia', with paddy plains around Alor Setar and the islands of Langkawi offshore.

Kelantan.lore: Home of the wau bulan, the moon kite on the 50 sen coin, flown at kite festivals on the east coast.

Malacca.lore: UNESCO old port city; the Porta de Santiago gate of the Portuguese fort A Famosa still stands.

Negeri Sembilan.lore: Minangkabau heritage: curved, horn-shaped roofs like the Istana Lama at Seri Menanti.

Pahang.lore: Tea terraces of the Cameron Highlands, plus Taman Negara, one of the oldest rainforests in the world.

Penang.lore: Street food capital: char kway teow and the street art and shophouses of George Town (UNESCO).

Perak.lore: The Kinta Valley once produced much of the world's tin; Ipoh grew rich on it.

Perlis.lore: Malaysia's smallest state, famous for the sweet Harumanis mango.

Sabah.lore: Mount Kinabalu (4,095 m), the highest peak in Malaysia, and Borneo's orangutans and reefs.

Sarawak.lore: The 'Land of the Hornbills', with the Mulu caves and longhouses along its rivers.

Selangor.lore: Fireflies glow along the Selangor River at Kuala Selangor; Batu Caves is here too.

Terengganu.lore: Turtles nest on its beaches, and the Perhentian and Redang islands lie offshore.

Kuala Lumpur.lore: The capital, with the Petronas Twin Towers joined by their skybridge.

Putrajaya.lore: The planned administrative capital; the rose-tinted dome of Putra Mosque rises over the lake.

Labuan.lore: Island territory off Borneo and an offshore oil and gas hub.

Kuala Lumpur.note: The 452 m Petronas Twin Towers, the tallest twin skyscrapers in the world.

Putrajaya.note: The rose-granite Putra Mosque on Putrajaya Lake, beside the Prime Minister's office.

Gombak.note: The limestone Batu Caves temple, with its golden statue of Lord Murugan and 272 steps.

Kuala Selangor.note: Fireflies glow in the mangroves along the Selangor River at Kampung Kuantan.

Kota Bharu.note: The central market of Kota Bharu, where most traders are women.

Johor Bahru.note: The state mosque of 1900, overlooking the Johor Strait.

Pontian.note: Pineapple farms on the peat soils of Pontian.

Kinta.note: Ipoh, in the Kinta Valley, is the home of white coffee; cave temples sit in the limestone hills around it.

Larut dan Matang.note: Rain trees over the old tin-mining ponds of the Taiping Lake Gardens.

Cameron Highlands.note: Terraced tea plantations on the hills, around 1,500 m up.

Raub.note: Raub is famous for its Musang King durians.

Rompin.note: Tioman Island, off the east coast, is part of Rompin district.

Kuala Terengganu.note: The steel-and-glass Crystal Mosque on Wan Man island in the Terengganu River.

Besut.note: Boats leave Kuala Besut for the coral reefs of the Perhentian Islands.

Langkawi.note: The curved Sky Bridge hangs near the top of Gunung Mat Cincang.

Sandakan.note: Sepilok Orangutan Rehabilitation Centre, in the forest outside Sandakan.

Semporna.note: Semporna is the gateway to the reefs and turtles of Sipadan.

Kinabatangan.note: The floodplain forests of the Kinabatangan River shelter hornbills, proboscis monkeys and pygmy elephants.

Kuching.note: Kuching's cat statues play on the city's name ('kucing' is Malay for cat).

Miri.note: Malaysia's first oil well, drilled on Canada Hill in 1910.

Labuan.note: The largest Commonwealth war cemetery in Malaysia, for soldiers of the Second World War.
